subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Brain-Computer Interfaces: Bridging Mind and Machine
description: One-minute skill: Brain-Computer Interfaces: Bridging Mind and Machine.

hook.text: In 2024, a Neuralink implant let a paralyzed man control a computer cursor with his thoughts. He played chess online.

buildup.text: Brain-computer interfaces read electrical signals from neurons. Electrodes on or in the brain detect patterns tied to intentions.

discovery.text: Non-invasive BCIs use EEG headsets but have low resolution. Invasive implants read single neurons but require brain surgery.

twist.text: The brain treats implants as foreign objects. Scar tissue forms around electrodes within months, degrading signal quality.

climax.text: Flexible electrode arrays and wireless implants are improving longevity. The goal is a device that lasts decades, not months.

punchline.text: Think the command. The machine obeys. The interface is your neurons.

quiz.question: What limits the long-term effectiveness of invasive brain implants?
options: Battery technology cannot sustain the implant for more than a few weeks
Scar tissue forms around electrodes, degrading signal quality over months
The brain adapts to the implant's signals and stops responding to them
